Having children can bring love, joy, and a strong sense of purpose, but it also involves sleep deprivation, financial pressure, less personal time, and years of responsibility. The experience varies greatly depending on your children, support network, and circumstances.

There is no universally right number to have. Consider your desire to parent, health, finances, time, relationship, and available support. Choosing not to have children is also valid. cases.pea_output: Having children can be deeply joyful and meaningful, but it also brings exhaustion, financial pressure, and major changes to your time, relationships, and priorities. There is no universally right number to have. Consider your health, finances, support network, partnership, lifestyle, and how much time and energy you can offer each child; for some people that means none, for others one, two, or more. Choose what supports a loving, stable family life rather than following outside expectations.
